eam,sicut & Dominus ecclesiam. Quoniam
membra sumus corporis eiusde, ex carne e-
ius & ex ossibus eius. Interim tamen obser-
vatione dignū, quòd mulier non de pede vi-
ri sumpta est, ne à viro conteneretur, 1.Pet.3.
neq; de capite, ne viro dominaretur, 1.Tim.2.
Si enim maritus vincatur, & uxor domine-
tur, (dicit Augustinus in Psal.143.) pax per-
versa est. Si autem uxor marito dominanti
subijciatur, pax recta. Io. Iouianus scribit
cap.3. de Obed. lib.3. Quænam pax in illa
esse domo potest, in qua mulieris dominetur
appetitus? Neq;.n.aut induere omnes Scra-
tè possunt, aut ducendæ uxoris finis is est vi-
ro, ut patientia assuefcat, toleràdisq; clamorib.
Septimó propter unam & eandem spem
vocationis, qua & vir & mulier, abs-q; perfo-
narum acceptione vocati sunt ad hæredita-
tem gratiæ vitæ.Ephes.4.1.Pet.3.Si ergo spe-
rant coniuges se simul victuros[?] in summa pa-
ce & tranquillitate post hanc vitam in regno
Dei; cur non etiam hic ad momentum saltem
student pacificè viuere? At patientia illis est
opus, ut ubi voluntatem Dei peregerint, re-
portent promissionem, Hebr. 10. Neque e-
nim seruari unquam concordia, nisi per so-
lam patientiam valet, sicut Gregorius testa-
tu lib. Moral. 5. Crebrò namque in huma-
na actione nascitur, unde mentes hominum
vicissim à suavitate & dilectione separen-
tur. Et nisi ad adversa toleranda in animo[?]

page.notes: Running head is "NVPTIALES." as printed (the N-V ligature is hard to read exactly). Page number "251": the final numeral is slightly blurred and could be read as "25ı". The "3" in the references "1.Pet.3.", "cap.3.", "lib.3." and "Pet.3." is printed as a yogh-like form (ʒ); transcribed as 3. The word after "vi" in "victuros" has a ligature (ct) that is not fully clear, so it is marked [?]. The last word "in animo" appears as "in snimo"; the first letter looks like an s or a long-s-like form, so it is read as "animo" and marked [?]. The page ends mid-sentence, and the paragraph continues on the next page. Faint scan artefacts (dashes and a small mark) at the very bottom are not printed text and are left out. Text in the scan has u/v and i/j normalised per the convention; long s is written as plain s.
